newsitem.title: USA: Rain relieves dryness in Florida citrus belt.
newsitem.headline: Rain relieves dryness in Florida citrus belt.

text.p: Rain on Jan 9 helped relieve dryness in the Florida citrus belt last week, said Florida Agricultural Statistics Service.

Most growers and caretakers are using irrigation to maintain good tree condition. In the week ended Jan 12, there was some new growth, generated by warm temperatures in late December, most of which is on young trees in the southern part of the citrus belt, FASS said.
According to FASS, harvest of early and mid season oranges was active this week.
FASS reported an estimated 195,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended Jan 12, down from 594,000 boxes the previous week and 144,000 boxes in the week ended Dec 29.
An estimated 9,612,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended Jan 12, up from 8,872,000 boxes the prior week and 6,485,000 boxes the week ended Dec 29.
